description:
Structured output for a generated implementation ticket.

The downstream generate_criteria agent has its own job — it derives
observable acceptance criteria from the full formatted ticket.

context.description: The repository facts the implementation rests on, including the documentation sources consulted.
context.title: Context

openQuestions.description: Questions the ticket could not settle from the repository.
openQuestions.title: Openquestions

references.description: Locations in the repository the implementer starts from.

items.description: A reference to a specific location in the codebase.

location.description: Where in the repository this points: a file path, optionally with a line range or a symbol name.
location.title: Location

note.description: What the implementer needs to know about this location.
note.title: Note

items.title: CodeReference

references.title: References

requiredChanges.description: Every file the change must touch, one entry per file.

items.description: A single file-level change required to implement the ticket.

changeType.description: Whether the file is created, modified or deleted.
changeType.title: Changetype

description.description: What changes in this file, stated as an observable outcome.
description.title: Description

filePath.description: Repository-relative path of the file this change touches.
filePath.title: Filepath

rationale.description: Why this change is required by the task, not merely useful.
rationale.title: Rationale

items.title: FileChange

requiredChanges.title: Requiredchanges

sherlockFlags.description: Every flag the draft critic raised about why a part of this ticket exists rather than whether it works, carried out unchanged; empty when none was raised.

items.description:
One thing the critic flags for a supervisor's attention.

The channel the persona rewrite had to preserve: a finding about WHY a
component exists rather than whether it works — over-implementation,
machinery no measured failure justifies, a goal quietly substituted.
It is a typed, routable item because a flag that cannot be routed is a
persona artefact with a new name.

Distinct from the accept gate's ``SherlockFlag``, which anchors to a
criterion id: this one anchors to a passage of a drafted artifact,
which has no criteria yet.  Same wire field name on two producers,
two anchors, one definition each.

reason.description: Why it is flagged: the measured failure that would justify it and is absent, or the goal it serves that the task never asked for.
reason.title: Reason

subject.description: What is flagged: the component, claim, or decision the supervisor should look at, named precisely enough to find.
subject.title: Subject

items.title: CritiqueFlag

sherlockFlags.title: Sherlockflags

summary.description: What the change accomplishes, for a reader with no other context.
summary.title: Summary

title.description: One line naming what the ticket delivers.
title.title: Title

title: TicketDraftOutput
